items.title: 3. What existing tools already give, and where reuse stops
items.text:
Applied to example B. Reconstructed from each tool's documented schema.

Construct Graphify SCIP Kythe class TensileTestSpecimen fields and their types -[references, field]-> Length, Width, Area, ModulusOfElasticity ...tensile_test/TensileTestSpecimen#e_mod. variable node, typed edge to tapp def tensile_test_analysis(ds: TensileTestDataset) -> TensileTestDataset -[references, parameter_type]->, -[references, return_type]-> (). descriptor plus occurrences function node, signature via fn#builtin class TensileTestResult(TabularData) -[inherits]-> Relationship.is_implementation extends cross_section_area = width * thickness nothing nothing nothing e_mod = ModulusOfElasticity.from_pint(...) -[calls]-> from_pint from_pint(). ReadAccess, e_mod. WriteAccess anchor plus ref/call, anchor plus ref/writes slope, *_ = linregress(...) -[calls]-> linregress local 0 ref/call Length(value=100, unit=LengthUnit.milli_meter) -[calls]-> Length occurrence only ref/call

Optional is filtered as a typing container and float as annotation noise; ModulusOfElasticity survives.

Reuse them for the type skeleton. They are sufficient there and should not be rebuilt. Every class, every field, every field's declared type, parameter and return types, inheritance.

All three lack the same thing: intra-procedural dataflow. Kythe's ref/writes records that e_mod was written; nothing connects it to the reads that produced the value. Navigation does not need that edge, so none of them emit it.

Also lost by all three: the literal arguments. Length(value=100, unit=LengthUnit.milli_meter) reduces to a calls edge, discarding 100 and milli_meter. For a materials knowledge graph that is the payload.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: The reuse split
items.text:
Layer Supplier Identity, declarations, field types, inheritance SCIP for versioned symbols, or Graphify Intra-procedural dataflow Joern CPG REACHING_DEF edges, or python-graphs for a pure-Python CFG and DFG Typed-boundary provenance AWL Literal arguments, control flow, collapse AWL only

This is the concrete answer to "can we just reuse their output". For the first two rows, yes. The last two are unbuilt anywhere.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Part II: Principles
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 4. Graphify's principles, and the tooling embodying each
items.text:
Principle Embodied in Failure it prevents Cutoff as declaration, not code LanguageConfig, a dataclass of frozensets Cutoff becomes inspectable and diffable rather than buried in a walker One normalization authority graphify/ids.py "Three independent producers must agree on node IDs or the graph splits a single entity into disconnected ghost nodes" Observation before inference _SymbolResolutionFacts, resolved in a later pass Extraction never guesses; guessing becomes auditable Provenance in the data model confidence: EXTRACTED / INFERRED / AMBIGUOUS per edge (engine.py:29) Consumers can ask for only what was literally written Ambient vocabulary is not corpus vocabulary builtin, typing-container, annotation-noise and decorator-noise filters Builtins "become god-nodes accumulating spurious edges from every call site" Small closed relation vocabulary one references relation plus a role from REFERENCE_CONTEXTS (engine.py:18), validated at construction The schema cannot grow by accident Stages as total functions over plain data detect -> extract -> build_graph -> cluster -> analyze -> report -> export Any stage is replaceable and testable in isolation Deterministic by default tree-sitter for code, model only for prose, quarantined behind the AMBIGUOUS tier Probabilistic output cannot silently contaminate deterministic output

Quoted rationales are the authors' own comments in graphify/ids.py and graphify/extractors/base.py.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 5. AWL's own principles
items.text:
1. Language-agnostic serialization, now binding rather than aspirational.
  2. The AST is the document, and it round-trips to source.
  3. Semantics live in the context, not the extractor. One document, many RDF projections.
  4. Restriction is a goal. JSON Schema constrains which constructs and which calls are legal in a workflow domain.
  5. Types carry their own semantics. The resolved type defines meaning, and the developer never writes an IRI.

Principles 1, 3 and 5 have no counterpart in the indexing tools. Principle 2 is unusual across the entire field.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 6. Compatibility and tensions
items.text: Graphify principle Verdict Note Cutoff as declaration Adopt, extended AWL needs transparent and opaque type sets, plus a content-dependent condition: a call collapses if and only if its callee resolves to an annotated type One normalization authority Adopt wholesale More critical for AWL, whose identifiers are global IRIs, so a collision is a wrong assertion rather than a merged node Observation before inference Adopt wholesale The enabling change; nothing else works without it Provenance in the data model Adopt, different tooling See tension 2 Ambient versus corpus vocabulary Adopt, inverted contents See tension 3 Small closed relation vocabulary Adopt, corroborated by 2.2 AWL has better tooling for it: type-scoped contexts Stages as total functions Adopt wholesale Purely architectural Deterministic by default Adopt with care Section 9 introduces a probabilistic path; it must stay quarantined
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Tension 1: round-trip versus cutoff
items.text:
If the AST is the document, eliding nodes breaks unparse. The backparsable flag in src/awl/core.py is this tension left unresolved as a boolean.

Resolution: stop treating document and graph as one artefact. Keep the document complete, put the cutoff in the projection. RDF canonicalization normalizes layout away by design, so the RDF projection is explicitly lossy in reverse. That is coherent, and it is SCIP's transmission-versus-storage split, but it must be stated rather than assumed.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Tension 2: provenance in RDF
items.text:
A triple carries no attributes.

Option Strength Cost Named graphs Clean, standard, queryable per graph Needs quads; to_jsonld() emits one document today RDF-star Most expressive Uneven tool support Parallel inferred graph Simplest One bit only

Named graphs are recommended. Section 9 raises the stakes: once meaning can be retrofitted by a model, declared and inferred semantics must never be indistinguishable.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Tension 3: ambient vocabulary is domain-relative
items.text: Graphify lists dataclass in _PYTHON_DECORATOR_NOISE as "ambient vocabulary, not corpus symbols". For AWL it is the primary identity signal. The principle transfers, the contents invert. Adopting the lists verbatim would be worse than having none.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Part III: Design
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 7. Language-agnostic vocabulary, with CPG as blueprint
items.text:
Correction worth stating first: tree-sitter does not normalize across languages. It is many parsers with different node vocabularies (function_definition in Python, function_declaration in JS, method_definition in TS). Graphify's LanguageConfig is a thin normalization layer mapping those names onto four roles. The normalization AWL wants is CPG's.

Joern's Code Property Graph is explicitly "a language-agnostic intermediate graph representation of code designed for code querying", one layered schema across all frontends. Six mechanisms transfer.

  1. Neutral core vocabulary. METHOD, BLOCK, CALL, CONTROL_STRUCTURE, IDENTIFIER, LITERAL, LOCAL, RETURN, TYPE_DECL, TYPE, MEMBER. Close to exactly what AWL's workflow profile needs, and none of it Python-specific.
  2. Terminology neutrality. Procedures, functions and methods are all METHOD. BLOCK rather than "compound statement", because blocks yield values in some languages.
  3. One node type plus discriminator. CONTROL_STRUCTURE carries a type property rather than spawning If, While, For classes.
  4. Escape hatch. UNKNOWN covers "any AST node that the frontend would like to include in the AST but for which no suitable AST node is specified".
  5. Raw frontend labels as properties, not types. PARSER_TYPE_NAME stores the "AST node type name emitted by parser", explicitly not used for control-flow construction.
  6. Declared language-specific dimensions. A LANGUAGE property names the frontend; SIGNATURE has no strict format "so it can be chosen by the frontend implementor to fit the source language"; for FULL_NAME, "the details of what constitutes a fully-qualified name are language specific".
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: This resolves tension 1
items.text: Mechanisms 4 and 5 let AWL keep a language-neutral vocabulary and round-trip Python exactly, because the Python-specific label rides as a property while the node type stays neutral. Vocabulary choice and frontend choice become independent, so principle 1 does not force a move to tree-sitter.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Joern as second frontend, not a replacement
items.text:
pysrc2cpg already emits the neutral vocabulary plus REACHING_DEF dataflow, which is the gap identified in section 3. Roughly the whole workflow profile, for free.

Caveats: Joern is JVM and Scala, heavy for a Python library, and CPG does not round-trip to source. So do not replace AWL's frontend with it. Two frontends, one vocabulary: Python ast for round-trip fidelity, exported CPG for breadth and dataflow.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Sanity check against non-Python source
items.text:
function procedure(cycles: number): void {
  let i = 0;
  while (i < cycles) { charge(new ChargeParam(4.2, 0.23)); rest(600); i += 1; }
}
Python ast TypeScript Neutral vocabulary FunctionDef function_declaration METHOD body list statement_block BLOCK Assign lexical_declaration CALL <operator>.assignment While while_statement CONTROL_STRUCTURE type While Call call_expression CALL Call ClassName(...) new_expression CALL, collapsed AugAssign augmented_assignment_expression CALL <operator>.assignmentPlus arg cycles: int required_parameter METHOD_PARAMETER_IN plus TYPE

Two findings. Call and new_expression are distinct in their grammars and identical semantically, which is mechanism 3 earning its keep. And Python keyword arguments have no TypeScript equivalent, so the collapse's input shape differs by language while its output does not. The collapse must therefore be defined over the resolved callee's parameter names, not over the source's keyword syntax. That is why 2.3's ARGUMENT_INDEX and ARGUMENT_NAME split matters.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 8. Identity
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Base scheme
items.text:
1. Detect the definition: a ClassDef carrying @dataclass or an OO-LD base.
  2. Mint from the fully qualified name under a configurable module-to-namespace mapping. Adopt Kythe's vnames.json pattern: identity minting is declarative configuration mapping path patterns to identity fields, not code.
  3. Carry a language or scheme dimension, per Kythe's VName language and SCIP's scheme.
  4. Carry an optional version component, per SCIP, or pin the environment instead, per PWD (2.8). Choose deliberately; do not do both. An FQN identifies a name, not a contract.
  5. Derive properties from the class body's annotated assignments.
  6. Resolve call sites through import facts. Do not write the resolver: Scalpel's FQN Inferrer and PyCG exist. Scalpel was last pushed 2024-03-28 (verified).
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Failure modes
items.text: Mode Solved by Action Re-exports Kythe emits both aliases and aliases/root Emit the alias hop and the resolved-to-root target so queries pick their indirection level. The likeliest source of duplicate nodes in Python Aliases Local import table Straightforward Overloads SCIP method-disambiguator Required, see below Version drift SCIP version component or PWD environment file Point 4 Star imports Nothing, anywhere Make import * illegal in the domain schema. This is what the restriction objective is for
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Identity is the typed instantiation, not the function
items.text:
The important refinement, and the mechanism that makes example B tractable.

scipy.stats.linregress is generic linear regression. Attaching (LinearStrain, Stress) -> ModulusOfElasticity to that identifier asserts it globally, so every other use of linregress inherits it. The semantics belong not to the function but to its typed instantiation:

scipy.stats.linregress                        no semantics, ever
scipy.stats.linregress(LinearStrain, Stress)  -> ModulusOfElasticity

This is functools.singledispatch semantics, and it is what SCIP's method-disambiguator and Kythe's opaque signature field exist for.

The payoff is large. With OO-LD types on the arguments, the typed instantiation is derivable statically at every call site. A model is needed once, to propose the mapping; dispatch afterwards is deterministic.

Retroactive minting. Kythe's entry store is append-only facts keyed by VName, so any analyzer may add facts about a symbol later and they join everywhere it was referenced. AWL should adopt the same property: mint the identifier for an opaque callee now, attach semantics whenever they become known, and every prior reference gains meaning without reprocessing. This is the architectural reason identity must be stable and global before anything else is built.

Dimensional analysis validates a proposed instantiation for free. Strain is dimensionless, so Stress / LinearStrain has dimension Pa, consistent with ModulusOfElasticity. Any proposed signature failing the dimensional check is rejected without executing anything. Deterministic, cheap, and it catches a large error class before section 9's expensive machinery runs.

Two complications visible in example B:

Arity. slope, *_ = linregress(...) discards four values; linregress returns five. The annotation target is a result schema, not a return type: .slope : ModulusOfElasticity, .rvalue : CorrelationCoefficient. More work, more reusable, and a natural fit for OO-LD.

The units are stripped before the call. The arguments are linear["strain"].pint.to_base_units().pint.magnitude, that is, dimensionless float arrays. (LinearStrain, Stress) describes values three attribute accesses upstream. The typed boundary is not at the call site, and AWL must trace back through a third-party wrapper chain to recover it. This is the hardest concrete case in the example and it should be treated as the acceptance test for any implementation.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 9. What AWL actually extracts, and how far down
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Typed boundaries, not operation semantics
items.text:
dataset.specimen.e_mod = ModulusOfElasticity.from_pint(slope.to("Pa"))

Whatever opaque computation produced slope, at the moment it is assigned to a typed member it acquires meaning. The same holds in reverse when a typed member is read out of an input argument. Typed members form a lattice of crossings: computation between crossings is opaque, meaning is recovered at every crossing, and there are many crossings per function rather than one per signature.

That is strictly more than signature-level annotation, and it is the precise sense in which AWL sees "inside" a function.

State the limit honestly. What is recovered is typed-boundary provenance: e_mod depends on width, thickness, length, force, elongation. The operation is not recovered. "Linear regression over the elastic region" is unavailable unless the callee's typed instantiation is known (section 8) or a model reads the code (below).

One genuine exception, and it is worth building on: width * thickness where both operands are typed quantities has a dimensionally derivable result type. That is real operation semantics, statically decidable, and unmatched by any project surveyed.

Claim Delivered Semantics of arbitrary operations No Typed-boundary provenance at many points per function Yes Result type of arithmetic over typed quantities Yes, by dimensional analysis Meaning of third-party numerics Only via a registered typed instantiation
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Retrofitting meaning onto untyped code
items.text:
The untyped end of the gradient. Plain or partially typed code yields hints; a model can propose meaning; the extraction is expensive, so it must be persisted against a global target and shared across repositories rather than recomputed per consumer.

OO-LD is a good target for a reason that is easy to miss: because the model's task is not "choose a vocabulary" (open-ended, unverifiable) but "choose a profile schema from a registry" (closed, validatable, recorded as a versioned $id). The output is a schema URL plus an instance, and both are checkable.

Validation, cheapest first:

Stage Cost Catches Dimensional analysis of the proposed signature Free, deterministic Large class of wrong types Schema validation of instances Cheap Structural errors Execution against literature reference data Expensive Wrong labels, semantically Cross-repository agreement on the same schema Ongoing Idiosyncratic mappings

Literature cross-validation is the strong step and deserves emphasis. Extract input and reported output from published work (a tensile test with attached plot or CSV and a reported E-modulus), run the schema-wrapped function, compare, repeat across independent sources. Unlike unit tests, the error sources are uncorrelated, so this validates the label, not merely the arithmetic.

Three limits to record:

  • Coverage is uneven. Only reported quantities get signal. cross_section_area and the 0.2 percent linear_region cutoff appear in no results table, so intermediates stay unvalidated. Confidence is high at the outputs and absent in the middle, which is where a retrofit is riskiest.
  • Convergence is on convention. If the field uses a 0.2 percent offset convention, cross-validation confirms the convention. That is the right outcome for interoperability and it makes the validated semantics explicitly community-relative.
  • The corpus is the asset. Paper-to-(input, reported output) pairs are expensive to assemble and outlast any pipeline built on them. Treat as a deliverable.

Retrofitted meaning must be distinguishable from declared meaning, permanently. This is where tension 2 stops being a nicety. Note also that a retrofit has no instance document to pin a versioned schema $id: the mapping lives in a generated annotation or a sidecar, so it needs its own version pin and provenance tier, or a temporary fallback vocabulary becomes indistinguishable from a consensus one once it propagates.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Why multiple vocabularies is a feature
items.text: A single global vocabulary is not achievable and not required. OO-LD carries a consensus mapping in the context while community synonyms ride along as structured annotations, so the consumer selects a mapping set rather than the producer enforcing one. That also accommodates a lazy or temporary vocabulary for freshly retrofitted code, upgraded later without rewriting instances. "One syntax, tiered semantics" is the correct answer to the global-target objection, subject to the version-pin caveat above.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 10. Graph semantics compared
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: A. Declarations-and-references level
items.text:
Where Graphify, Kythe, SCIP and Glean sit.

graph LR
  P[procedure.py] -->|imports| PP[battery/params.py]
  P -->|imports| PD[battery/device.py]
  F["procedure()"] -->|calls EXTRACTED| C["charge()"]
  F -->|calls EXTRACTED| R["rest()"]
  F -->|calls EXTRACTED| CP[ChargeParam]
  PP --> CP

Answers "does procedure use charge". Cannot answer "in what order", "how many times", "at what target voltage".
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: B. AWL ast profile
items.text:
Full tree, transparent wrappers unwrapped. Round-trips. Verbose.

graph LR
  M[Module] --> FD[FunctionDef procedure]
  FD --> WH[While]
  WH --> EX[Expr]
  EX --> CA["Call charge"]
  CA --> CA2["Call ChargeParam"]
  CA2 --> KW["keyword target_voltage"]
  KW --> CO["Constant 4.2"]
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: C. AWL workflow profile
items.text:
The recommended level, using section 7's vocabulary and section 12's alignments.

graph LR
  PR["awl:Method<br/>py:procedure#procedure"] -->|parameter| PA["cycles : builtins.int"]
  PR -->|body order 0| S1["awl:Call <operator>.assignment<br/>i = 0"]
  PR -->|body order 1| W["awl:ControlStructure type=While"]
  W -->|condition| CD["i < cycles"]
  W -->|body order 0| S3["fno:Execution<br/>fno:executes py:battery.device.charge"]
  W -->|body order 1| S4["fno:Execution<br/>fno:executes py:battery.device.rest"]
  W -->|body order 2| S5["awl:Call <operator>.assignmentPlus<br/>i += 1"]
  S3 -->|declared predicate| CPI["a py:battery.params.ChargeParam<br/>target_voltage 4.2<br/>c_rate 0.23"]
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: D. Typed-boundary provenance, example B
items.text:
What sections 8 and 9 buy on the real case.

graph LR
  W["specimen.width : Width"] --> A["specimen.cross_section_area : Area"]
  T["specimen.thickness : Length"] --> A
  A --> ST["df.stress : Stress"]
  FO["row.force : Force"] --> ST
  EL["row.elongation : Length"] --> SR["df.strain : LinearStrain"]
  L["specimen.length : Length"] --> SR
  SR --> LRlinregress<br/>opaque unless registered
  ST --> LR
  LR --> EM["specimen.e_mod : ModulusOfElasticity"]

Every node is a typed member; every edge is a provenance dependency recovered at a crossing. The single opaque node is the one section 8 registers as a typed instantiation, and dimensional analysis confirms Stress / LinearStrain yields Pa.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 11. The context lever
items.text: What AWL has and the indexing tools structurally lack. All claims here were reproduced locally against rdflib and pyld.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Ordering, at more than one layer
items.text:
@container: @list produces a genuine RDF collection. JSON-LD 1.1 API section 8.3: "List Conversion is the process of taking a list object and transforming it into an RDF collection as defined in RDF Semantics."

[] a :Method ;
    :body ( [ a :Call ; :callee "charge" ]
            [ a :Call ; :callee "rest" ]
            [ a :Call ; :callee "increment" ] ) .

?m awl:body/rdf:rest*/rdf:first ?step retrieves all three (verified). But it yields members, not positions: recovering an index means counting rdf:rest hops, and SPARQL 1.1's property path grammar has only *, + and ?. Result order is a store artefact, not a guarantee.

Emit both: @container: @list for fidelity, since it costs nothing and round-trips, and a materialized integer index as the query surface. Optionally derive p-plan:isPreceededBy in the plan projection. Keep 2.3's two orderings separate.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Numeric round-trip, and where it actually bites
items.text:
JSON-LD 1.1 API section 8.6 warns that "when JSON-native numbers are deserialized to RDF, lossless data round-tripping cannot be guaranteed", and that an xsd:double of 2.0 "will result in an xsd:integer with a value of 2 in canonical lexical form when converted from RDF to JSON-LD and back to RDF".

This does not currently bite awl-python. Both rdflib and pyld preserve 4.0 as xsd:double (verified), because Python's json module parses 4.0 to float and 4 to int.

JavaScript cannot: JSON.parse('4.0') and JSON.parse('4') both yield 4, and Number.isInteger is true for both (verified, Node v25.6.0). A JavaScript processor must emit xsd:integer.

So the hazard is cross-language, exactly the axis principle 1 cares about. A parameter written target_voltage=4.0 survives a Python round-trip and silently becomes an integer through a JavaScript one. Precision loss is real in both: 1.234567890123456789 returns as 1.234567890123457 (verified), the canonical form rounding the mantissa to 15 digits.

Mitigation verified: coercing the term fixes the datatype regardless of native value.

{"@context": {"v": {"@id": "http://ex.org/v", "@type": "xsd:double"}}, "v": 4}

emits "4.0E0"^^xsd:double; without coercion the same input emits "4"^^xsd:integer.

Type numeric terms explicitly, derived from the field annotations AWL already reads. And state plainly that the authoritative round-trip is document to source, never RDF to source.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Term rescue via embedded context
items.text:
A fallback @vocab makes unmapped keys expand rather than drop. For a collapsed type the namespace is unknown when the context is authored, so post-processing emits an embedded @context on that node object. JSON-LD 1.1 permits a context at any node object. Verified:

[] a :Call ;
    :callee <https://w3id.org/awl/py/battery.device.charge> ;
    :hasArgument [ a <https://w3id.org/awl/py/battery.params.ChargeParam> ;
            ns1:c_rate 2.3e-01 ;
            ns1:target_voltage 4.2e+00 ] .

with ns1 bound to the type's namespace. This is what makes the collapse lossless.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Disambiguation via type-scoped contexts
items.text: One term meaning different things under different node types: args under a method declaration is a parameter list, under a call an argument list; a name under an annotation is a type, elsewhere a variable. This is AWL's answer to the closed-vocabulary principle and stronger than a qualifier enum, because disambiguation is declarative and per-type. It is also the feature LinkML's generator does not emit, and therefore OO-LD's clearest differentiator.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 12. Alignment targets
items.text:
• FnO for call semantics: fno:Execution, fno:executes, per-parameter fno:predicate, at minimum as owl:equivalentProperty mappings. Language-neutral, which principle 1 requires.
  • P-Plan for the plan layer, PROV-O for the trace layer. AWL's TBox and ABox union is P-Plan's structure already.
  • PROV-O derivation for the section 9 provenance edges specifically, since typed-boundary provenance is prov:wasDerivedFrom at sub-function granularity.
  • CPG's schema for the neutral node vocabulary, per section 7.
  • PMDco, BFO, OBI and QUDT if AWL targets materials science; semantikon has validated these choices in that domain. QUDT covers units, which example B needs and the AWL vocabulary does not address. Not exclusive with FnO: FnO covers the call, PMDco the quantities.
  • RO-Crate conformsTo for declaring which restriction profile a document claims, and Workflow Run RO-Crate's Provenance Run Crate for packaging execution traces (section 14).
  • Glean's codemarkup pattern: define the workflow projection as derived rules (SPARQL CONSTRUCT or SHACL) over language-specific base facts. This is also how a second frontend stays cheap.
  • JSON Schema versus SHACL: do not duplicate. Document-shaped constraints to JSON Schema as an authoring-time gate; path-shaped-across-the-graph to SHACL.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 13. Cutoff design
items.text:
Profiles over one pipeline, replacing the backparsable boolean.

Profile Contents Diagram ast Transparent wrappers and empty lists elided, everything else kept B workflow Control flow, calls, assignments, literal arguments; non-call expressions collapse to a source-text literal C provenance Typed boundaries and their dependencies only D signature Declaration inputs and outputs only close to A

Round-trip fidelity is an orthogonal axis and must be separated from level.

AWL's cutoff is content-dependent: a call collapses if and only if its callee resolves to an annotated type. That is strictly more expressive than CodeOntology's binary flag, the only precedent for a cutoff knob, and it is what makes the gradient in 2.8 possible.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Part IV: Execution tracing
items.text: Everything above concerns the static plan. This part concerns instantiation: what actually ran, along which path, with which values.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 14. Plan and trace
items.text:
The scientific workflow community already has the vocabulary:

Term Status in AWL-LD The recipe prospective provenance Parts I to III The run retrospective provenance This part

Bridge: p-plan:Activity with p-plan:correspondsToStep, plus prov:used and prov:generated.

The observation that reconciles AWL-LD's control flow with the dataflow ecosystem: a trace is always a DAG, even when the plan contains loops and branches. A loop of N iterations becomes N activities; a branch resolves to exactly one path. So control flow lives in the plan, and the trace is the unrolled dataflow DAG that CWL, PROV, P-Plan and PWD already model. AWL-LD sits upstream of those vocabularies rather than competing with them, which removes the apparent conflict noted in 2.5.

Two things a trace needs that PROV does not supply: a stable identity per plan step (section 8, again) and an iteration ordinal. PROV has no loop counter.

For packaging a run, Workflow Run RO-Crate provides three nested profiles under w3id.org/ro/wfrun/:

Profile Records Process Run Crate Tool executions as CreateAction, implicit workflow Workflow Run Crate Adds a ComputationalWorkflow instrument and FormalParameter slots. Individual step executions are not represented Provenance Run Crate Adds per-step CreateAction entities and intermediate outputs

Provenance Run Crate is the target. It reuses the conformsTo convention already recommended in section 12.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 15. How the ecosystem handles branching
items.text:
Library Conditional Loop CWL when on a step, added in v1.2 only, plus pickValue Not in the standard. cwltool:Loop extension only, and it cannot be combined with scatter or when in the same step WDL if scatter only, no while Snakemake Resolved at DAG construction, not at runtime Same PWD None None P-Plan, PROV None None AiiDA if_ in the WorkChain outline while_, with a checkpoint per iteration aiida-workgraph Explicit If, While and Map zones in the graph Same jobflow Response(replace=, detour=, addition=) at runtime Same Prefect Native Python Native Python Joern CPG CONTROL_STRUCTURE plus CFG and CDG edges Same

Two numbers worth keeping: of the 43 Workflow Patterns Initiative control patterns, CWL v1.2 supports 8 and does not support 35, and exclusive choice must be emulated by giving one step the inverse when condition of another.

The decisive finding: AiiDA has real control flow but keeps it out of its provenance graph. Its documentation states the branch and iteration logic itself is not a node; provenance captures the data and processes actually created. So "which branch was taken" is first-class nowhere.

The pattern across the table is that static languages omit branching while orchestrators expand it away at runtime. Both ends avoid representing the branch itself. That is the gap, and section 16 shows AWL-LD's draft already fills it.

Scope warning: 35 unsupported patterns shows how deep this goes. Do not chase the Workflow Patterns catalogue. Python's ast bounds the problem usefully already: If, While, For, Try, With, Break, Continue.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 16. The existing trace draft, assessed
items.text:
The awl-schema README already contains a tracing draft: sys.settrace events serialized as a steps list, each entry carrying func, lineno, locals, os, timestamp and type, with a code back-reference of the form {_type, lineno}.

It is conceptually ahead of the field.

Feature Note steps with @container: @list Already the ordering choice recommended in section 11 Branch resolution The If appears as a line event and subsequent events reveal the taken path Loop iterations The While recurs with changed locals. Nothing else in the survey records this code: {_type, lineno} Independently reinvents p-plan:correspondsToStep Variable-level state locals at every line event is finer than any WMS; AiiDA and CWL capture step inputs and outputs only Environment declared out of scope Correct, and it matches how WRROC separates buildInstructions from the run

Seven gaps.

  1. lineno is a fragile join key. Edit the file and every historical trace orphans. Kythe's design is instructive: the anchor is deliberately the volatile part and the VName is durable. The draft has only the volatile part.
  2. func is a bare name under ex:. Same god-node problem as the static side; two functions named run in different modules collapse.
  3. No iteration ordinal. The two While events differ only by list position, so every query becomes a list traversal. Same fix as section 11: materialize an index.
  4. locals is a snapshot, not a derivation. Diffing adjacent events infers change, but there is no prov:wasDerivedFrom. Trace size is O(lines x locals).
  5. Values are captured as literals. A local holding a ModulusOfElasticity should serialize as that typed node, not as repr(). This is where the trace layer and the collapse of section 9 should meet and currently do not. It is the highest-value fix, because it is what makes a trace semantic rather than a log.
  6. Parallel vocabulary. awl:WorkflowRun, awl:HasStep, awl:calls and awl:Parameters are minted where prov:Activity, prov:used, p-plan:correspondsToStep and the WRROC CreateAction shape exist.
  7. os: {cores: 8} repeats on every event. Static environment belongs once on the run.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 17. Instrumentation mechanics
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: The existing test implementation
items.text:
osw-chatbot/src/osw_chatbot/tests/ast_.py (78 lines, 2025-03-27) is a working trace-to-AST mapping. test2.py beside it is its predecessor, capturing f_locals to YAML with no AST mapping.

A trace event exposes only f_lineno, never a column, so it packs both into the line number before compiling:

n.lineno = n.lineno * 1000 + n.col_offset
code = compile(a, '', 'exec')

That buys expression-level resolution. Verified on b = a + 2:

raw f_lineno decoded AST node 3004 line 3, col 4 a 3008 line 3, col 8 2 3004 line 3, col 4 BinOp a + 2 3000 line 3, col 0 Assign

One bug, confirmed by running it. The decode reuses the divided value:

line_no = frame.f_lineno
line_no = line_no // 1000       # line_no overwritten
col_offset = line_no % 1000     # modulo of the already-divided value

so col_offset always equals line_no. Keep the raw value instead:

raw = frame.f_lineno
line_no, col_offset = raw // 1000, raw % 1000

The file's closing comment also records a real finding worth preserving: coverage.py was evaluated and rejected because CoverageData does not store the called lines in order.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: The hack is obsolete on Python 3.11
items.text:
PEP 657 added co_positions() in 3.11. Setting frame.f_trace_opcodes = True and indexing co_positions() at f_lasti // 2 reproduces the same sub-expression sequence on unmodified source. Verified on b = a + 2:

('opcode', (1, 1, 4, 5))    -> a
('opcode', (1, 1, 8, 9))    -> 2
('opcode', (1, 1, 4, 9))    -> a + 2
('opcode', (1, 1, 0, 1))    -> b
lineno packing co_positions() Requires AST rewrite and recompile Yes No Works on installed third-party code No Yes Column cap 999 None End position No Yes, full (lineno, end_lineno, col, end_col) span

The third-party row is the unlock: the packing trick only ever sees code compiled by the tracer itself, which is why library internals were invisible. The end span matters too, because a full span maps onto an AST node exactly where a start offset alone is ambiguous.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: C functions are visible
items.text:
settrace does not see them. sys.setprofile does, and yields the fully qualified name directly as arg.__module__ + "." + arg.__qualname__:

('c_call', 'numpy',    'array')
('c_call', 'math',     'sqrt')
('c_call', 'builtins', 'len')

Both hooks can be active simultaneously, which attributes a C call to an AST node. Verified:

('AST', 3, 4)                    <- Call node math.sqrt(2)
('C-CALL', 'math.sqrt')          <- attributed here
('AST', 4, 4)
('C-CALL', 'builtins.len')

Limits: arg is the function object, so no arguments, and no position of its own. The position comes entirely from the interleaved trace event.

This is the runtime counterpart to section 8's retroactive mint: setprofile names the opaque callee, and semantics can be attached to that name later.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Three instrumentation strategies
items.text:
Strategy Granularity Overhead Blind to settrace plus opcode positions Expression High C functions setprofile Call, including C Medium Positions, arguments Decorator (Prefect, AiiDA, jobflow) Task boundary Negligible Everything undecorated

They compose rather than compete. Prefect is the pure decorator case: it never inspects code and records only what is decorated, so the DAG is discovered at runtime and nothing undecorated exists. Prefect 3's prefect.telemetry.run_telemetry emits a span per run with run metadata as attributes, state changes as events and traceparent propagated via run labels, but task input and output values are not span attributes, so there is no data lineage by default.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: sys.monitoring (PEP 669), and what it costs
items.text:
Loss versus settrace Detail No frame object Every callback is (code, instruction_offset, ...). No frame, no documented route to locals. sys._getframe() works but negates the performance gain. This directly blocks the draft's locals capture No columns on LINE LINE is func(code, line_number) alone; only other events carry instruction_offset, so co_positions() cannot be reached from LINE Per-interpreter, not per-thread Stated in the PEP as a difference from settrace Python 3.12+ Hard floor Expensive reconfiguration set_events mid-run triggers de-optimization, "possibly taking hundreds of milliseconds" Memory per code object ~40% for LINE with one tool, ~80% for INSTRUCTION, ~120% and ~200% with two or more Six tool IDs 0 to 5, conventionally 0 debugger, 1 coverage, 2 profiler, 5 optimizer

Gains that matter here: a BRANCH event carrying destination_offset, which records the taken path directly instead of by diffing line events; a unified CALL event with signature (code, instruction_offset, callable, arg0) covering Python and C callables and supplying the first argument, which is strictly more than setprofile gives; per-event opt-in so LINE can be skipped entirely; and coexistence with settrace and setprofile, which behave "as if they were tools 6 and 7".

Conclusion: adopt sys.monitoring for BRANCH and CALL, not as a settrace replacement. Keep settrace alongside for the frame access that locals capture requires. The PEP explicitly supports running both.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Part V: Visual editing
items.text: A third consumer of the same document: a graph editor that renders and edits workflows and writes them back as Python. This part asks how compact the representation can get, what fidelity survives the round trip, and which libraries fit.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 18. Compact representation
items.text:
Measured on example A, round-trip verified identical to source.

Form Bytes % of raw ast2json raw 4386 100% Current awl, positions and ctx stripped 1689 39% Compact form 1056 24% The Python source itself 242 6%

The compact encoding is four rules:

_type       ->  _
Constant    ->  {"c": value}
Name        ->  {"$": id}
drop ctx, all position fields, None values, and empty lists

Compactness is a property of the encoder and decoder pair, not of the document. Dropping empty lists alone fails: Module.type_ignores is required, so unparse raises AttributeError. The decoder must rebuild every required field from cls._fields, exactly as unparse() in src/awl/core.py already re-adds lineno: 0. There is no compact form that survives a naive decoder.

Residual bloat against source is 4.4x, almost entirely {"_": ...} type tags and the arguments, arg, alias and keyword wrapper nodes. Those are precisely the transparent wrappers of section 7, and collapsing keyword into a dict on the Call is the existing slim notation generalised.

The editor encoding and the cutoff design are the same problem. The transparent and opaque type sets defined for the projection also define the compact form. Do not solve them twice.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 19. Round-trip fidelity and write-back
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: ast.unparse discards trivia
items.text:
ast.parse has no comment node at all, so every comment and all formatting is lost:

def procedure(cycles: int) -> None:
    # ramp to 4.2 V, CC phase only                     <- gone
    while i < cycles:
        charge(ChargeParam(target_voltage=4.2,   # cell limit per datasheet   <- gone
                           c_rate=0.23))              <- reflowed to one line

For workflows authored in the editor this is irrelevant. For editing a laboratory's existing procedure files it is fatal, and that is the audience the retrofit path of section 9 targets. It is also the practical face of tension 1: "the AST is the document and it round-trips" is true only modulo trivia, and a visual editor is where users notice.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: CST, and why the choice is not a fork
items.text:
A Concrete Syntax Tree keeps everything the parser saw.

AST (ast) CST (parso, libcst, tree-sitter) Comments No node type exists Preserved Whitespace and indentation Discarded Preserved Redundant parentheses (a + b) identical to a + b Distinct Quote style Both Constant('x') Distinct Round-trip Lossy Byte-identical (verified: parso.parse(src).get_code() == src)

You do not have to choose between the compact form and trivia preservation. Keep the compact AST JSON as the editor model, never serialize a CST, and write edits back by source span. Verified with asttokens, already installed: locate the target_voltage value node, ask for its span (145, 148), splice the new literal into the original text. Both comments survive and layout is untouched.

The span machinery already exists in the design: section 17 needs co_positions() spans to attribute trace events, and the same tuples identify the patch target. One mechanism, two consumers. It also needs no unparser, only spans plus original text, so it works identically for tree-sitter, which removes the round-trip objection to a tree-sitter frontend raised in section 4.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Where spans stop and libcst starts
items.text:
Span splicing has no opinion about which comment belongs to which statement, so reordering or reparenting a node cannot carry its trivia. libcst attaches trivia to named slots (leading_lines, trailing_whitespace) and handles it. Verified with libcst 1.9.0:

  • parse_module(src).code == src byte-identical.
  • A new statement can be constructed carrying modeled comments, leading and trailing, and emitted into source.
  • Inserting that statement into a while body leaves every original comment and the original odd spacing untouched.
  • Comments extract back into the model: leading comments attach to the following statement, trailing to the same line.

So a comment field in the editor is not a workaround, it is the right design. Modeled comments round-trip in both directions. Two limits found, both model decisions rather than bugs:

  • A comment inside call arguments attaches to an inner expression node, not to the statement. A per-step comment field captures statement-level comments only; expression-level trivia is preserved but not editable.
  • A section banner and a commented-out line arrive identically as leading comments. Attachment is positional, so do not try to classify them; keep an ordered list per step.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: The resulting rule
items.text: Operation Fidelity Edit a literal or parameter Lossless via asttokens spans, no new dependency Add, delete or reorder steps Lossless via libcst Regenerate a whole file from the graph Lossy by construction, and say so
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 20. Editor architecture
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Paradigm before library
items.text:
Node-graph editors model dataflow; block editors model control flow. AWL-LD's differentiator against CWL, PWD and semantikon is that it carries if and while. React Flow makes a nested loop body awkward, needing group nodes or subflow conventions; Blockly represents nested statements natively with C-shaped blocks and already ships a Python generator. Choosing a node-graph canvas quietly pushes the model back toward the dataflow shape section 2.5 says the ecosystem already occupies.

This is a product decision, and it is the same decision as whether control flow is the differentiator.

Layer Option Verdict Canvas, control-flow-first Blockly Native nested statements, existing Python generator. Weak at data dependencies; embedding a rich form in a block is awkward Canvas, dataflow-first React Flow (xyflow) Custom React nodes are trivial, largest ecosystem. Loops need group conventions Rete.js, LiteGraph, Drawflow More opinionated or smaller, no advantage here Read-only graph view Cytoscape.js Right tool for the derived RDF and trace graphs: large graphs, real layout algorithms vis-network, D3 vis-network is easiest but weak at scale; D3 means building it yourself Python bridge anywidget Already used in oold-python/src/oold/ui/anywidget/; works in Jupyter, Panel, marimo and JupyterLite/pyodide Panel ReactComponent Present in the installed panel 1.7.5, with JSComponent and AnyWidgetComponent NiceGUI Server-side Vue, rules out JupyterLite

Do not make one library do both editing and graph analysis. Different jobs, different layout needs.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Schema-driven form: jedison over RJSF
items.text:
jedison 1.19.0 react-jsonschema-form Runtime dependencies Zero, no dependencies or peerDependencies, not even a validator React, @rjsf/validator-ajv8 (ajv), a theme package Drafts Explicit modules for 04, 06, 07, 2019-09, 2020-12 via ajv8 Conformance testing Official json-schema-test-suite in devDeps ajv's $ref Own ref-parser, exported as RefParser via ajv Widget selection x-format inside the schema uiSchema, a separate object Editors shipped 40+, including if-then-else, multiple for anyOf/oneOf, object-categories, object-nav, array-table, plus ace, milkdown, flatpickr, imask Core widgets plain; rich ones from theme packages Stars, license, activity 88, MIT, pushed 2026-08-13, 1261 commits 15871, Apache-2.0, actively maintained

Other exports: Schema, Utils, Create, SchemaGenerator, applyOverlay.

The decisive argument is a principle argument. RJSF's uiSchema is a second artifact. OO-LD exists because keeping structure and semantics in two files makes them drift; a separate uiSchema reintroduces exactly that drift for the presentation layer. jedison's x-format lives in the schema, the same in-schema extension pattern as x-oold-*, and applyOverlay supports the layered approach when it is wanted deliberately. Fair caveat: a uiSchema can be derived from x-oold-* at load time in about thirty lines, so this is a soft violation, but that mapping is a layer to own forever.

Two supporting points. This project is already on that codebase: OoldEditor imports @json-editor/json-editor and the AWL playground loads it too, and across two accounts jedison's author has 601 commits on json-editor against the original author's 315. So jedison is a migration and RJSF is a rewrite. And zero dependencies matters for the JupyterLite target that the HITL example explicitly names.

RJSF wins on React Flow embedding, since jedison is imperative DOM and needs a mount and unmount wrapper that survives React 18 StrictMode double-invocation; on bus factor, mitigated by MIT plus zero dependencies making vendoring trivial; and on TypeScript types.

The form library should follow the canvas decision. Blockly means no React, so jedison outright. React Flow makes RJSF the path of least resistance, though the jedison wrapper is still cheaper than a permanent uiSchema mapping.

Not yet verified: that @context and x-oold-* pass through jedison untouched. Both specifications require unknown keywords to be ignored and json-editor already handles these schemas, so the risk is low, but it deserves a test against a real OO-LD schema.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: What is actually new here
items.text:
Unparsing to Python is not new: Blockly generates Python, BlockPy does dual block and text editing for Python, Pencil Code is bidirectional, App Inventor has an ANTLR-based blocks-to-text converter, and JetBrains MPS is the deep precedent for projecting one AST into several notations.

Blockly, BlockPy Node-RED, KNIME, PyFlow AWL-LD Entry point Code authored in the tool The graph is the source of truth Arbitrary existing Python Editor model is also the RDF graph No No Yes Node palette Hand-authored block definitions Hand-authored Derived from the OO-LD schema

The third row is the strongest and least obvious: the same generator that produces forms and pydantic classes produces the palette, where every other editor requires a hand-written definition per construct.
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: Part VI: Conclusions
path: Deriving semantic graph from code: principles, prior art, and design for AWL-LD

items.title: 21. What is genuinely novel
items.text:
Narrowed against the survey, and narrower than an unexamined pitch would claim.

  1. AST-subtree collapse driven by a type-scoped context selected by the resolved callee. FnO reaches the same target from a different direction and semantikon is a live implementation of types-carry-semantics. What is unprecedented is only the mechanism: those attach semantics to a declared signature, whereas AWL rewrites a call site's AST subtree using the resolved callee's context. Claim the mechanism, not the goal.
  2. Progressive enhancement with no cliff. Every alternative is all-or-nothing per function (semantikon) or requires restructuring into a dataflow graph (PWD, CWL). AWL degrades continuously from plain code to fully typed. This is the strongest claim and the least obvious.
  3. Typed-boundary provenance at many points inside one function, rather than one annotation per signature, plus dimensional derivation of result types for arithmetic over typed quantities.
  4. One artifact serving three roles: round-trippable source document, semantic graph serialization, and visual editor model. srcML has the first; every code-to-RDF project has the second; Blockly and BlockPy have a form of the third but only over code authored in their own tool. Section 20 adds the part with no precedent at all: the editor palette is derived from the OO-LD schema, where every surveyed editor requires a hand-written block or node definition per construct.
  5. JSON Schema as whitelist of legal constructs and callees. CWL's requirements governs runtime capability; RO-Crate's conformsTo has the shape but no teeth. It is also the only sound answer to import *.
  6. Retroactive semantics via stable global identity: register the typed instantiation of an opaque callee once, and every prior reference gains meaning. Kythe's append-only entry model is the architectural precedent; nobody applies it to workflow semantics.
  7. RDF vocabulary for control flow in a workflow plan. Cautions: the ecosystem concluded imperative control flow is the wrong abstraction for a plan, so keep it in the source-fidelity layer and let the plan projection be dataflow; and BPMN-derived ontologies are the unsurveyed place to look.
  8. Recording which branch was taken and which iteration ran, as first-class trace data. Section 15 shows this exists nowhere: static languages omit branching, orchestrators expand it away at runtime, and AiiDA has real control flow but keeps branch and iteration logic out of its provenance graph. The draft in section 16 already does it. This is the retrospective counterpart to claim 7 and is at least as defensible.
  9. Expression-level trace-to-AST attribution, including opaque C callees. Section 17 shows the mechanism works today: opcode positions place each event on an AST node, and an interleaved setprofile names C functions the static analysis cannot see. No surveyed system attributes runtime events below the task boundary.

items.title: 22. Prioritised recommendations
items.text:
Priority Action Buys Costs 1 Neutral node vocabulary modelled on CPG, with PARSER_TYPE_NAME-style label preservation Language-agnostic graph without losing Python round-trip; unblocks any second frontend Vocabulary redesign, expensive to change later 2 Identity: FQN plus language, optional version, minted declaratively, with alias and alias-root pairs, and typed instantiation as the unit for callees Correct collapse, no ghost nodes, retroactive semantics Needs an import-resolution pass 3 Observation before inference: collect import and declaration facts, resolve separately Makes 2 auditable and re-runnable Refactor of core.py 4 Context lever: @list plus materialized index, embedded @vocab, explicit numeric typing, type-scoped disambiguation Fixes ordering, makes collapse lossless, closes the cross-language numeric hazard Cheapest item here 5 Reuse rather than rebuild: SCIP or Graphify for the type skeleton, Joern REACHING_DEF or python-graphs for dataflow Removes the largest build item from scope Integration and a CPG-to-RDF projection 6 Typed-boundary provenance, with the .pint.magnitude case as acceptance test The claim in 18.3 Requires 2, 3 and 5 7 FnO, P-Plan and PROV-O alignment Interoperability; avoids minting predicates that later need migrating Vocabulary mapping 8 Provenance via named graphs Declared and retrofitted meaning stay distinguishable Changes to_jsonld() to quads 9 Ambient-vocabulary filters, re-derived for workflows Removes god-nodes Lists built from scratch, not copied 10 Profile split Cutoff becomes a parameter Depends on 1 and 3

Items 1 and 2 come first: both are hard to change later, and both are prerequisites for a second frontend and for retroactive semantics.

Item 8 is not optional once section 9 is in scope. A retrofit pipeline that cannot mark its own output is worse than no retrofit pipeline.

items.title: M1 awl.vocab implementation plan
items.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

Goal: A language-neutral node vocabulary, the two orderings, the per-profile elision sets and the ambient-noise lists, as pure data, so the cutoff is a declaration rather than logic buried in a walker.

Architecture: Constants only, no behaviour. Modelled on Joern's Code Property Graph. Python-specific labels survive as a parserTypeName property rather than as node types.

Tech Stack: Python stdlib ast for the mapping keys. No dependency.

items.title: Contract
items.text: Consumes nothing Produces constants read by M5, M6, M7 Depends on awl.contracts only, and only for the profile names

items.title: Why not one RDF class per ast node type
items.text: Joern has no ASSIGNMENT node: x = y + 1 is a CALL named <operator>.assignment. CodeQL uses one exprs table keyed (parent, idx). CodeOntology minted a class per construct and was last pushed 2018-06-27. Beyond the maintenance evidence, a class-per-node vocabulary versions AWL-LD against the CPython grammar forever. Measured on 3.11.6: 27 statement types, 32 expression types, 13 binary operators, 10 comparison operators. The exact counts move between releases, which is the point.

items.title: The vocabulary
items.text:
Twelve node types. Nothing below is Python-specific.

Type Covers Method FunctionDef, AsyncFunctionDef, Lambda. Procedures, functions and methods are one type Block Module, and any statement-list body Call Call, and every operator ControlStructure If, While, For, AsyncFor, With, AsyncWith, Try, TryStar, Match, Break, Continue. Discriminated by a controlStructureType property, not by one class per construct Identifier Name Literal Constant, JoinedStr, FormattedValue Local a name bound in a method body Return Return, Yield, YieldFrom, Await TypeDecl ClassDef Type an annotation position Member AnnAssign at class scope Unknown anything unmapped, carrying parserTypeName

Operators become calls with a reserved name:

Python Call name Assign, AnnAssign <operator>.assignment AugAssign <operator>.assignmentPlus and siblings BinOp <operator>.addition, .subtraction, ... Compare <operator>.lessThan, .equals, ... Attribute <operator>.fieldAccess Subscript <operator>.indexAccess

items.title: The two orderings
items.text:
Verified against the CPG specification, and not optional: conflating them breaks the collapse boundary, which is where a call's keywords become a type's named properties.

Property Meaning order Syntactic sibling slot within an ordered statement list. Leftmost is 0 argumentIndex Binds a call-site argument to a callee parameter. Positional args are 1..N; -1 means the argument is named, and argumentName carries the name

order is also the materialized integer index that makes statement sequence queryable without rdf:rest*/rdf:first traversal. M5 emits both.

items.title: Profiles
items.text:
Three declared behaviours per profile, not two.

Profile Transparent (unwrapped) Folds keywords Opaque (one node, source text) ast nothing no nothing workflow Expr, arguments, alias yes BinOp, BoolOp, UnaryOp, Compare provenance Expr, arguments, alias yes as workflow, plus non-boundary calls signature Expr, arguments, alias yes as workflow, plus all bodies

ast elides nothing structural. An earlier draft made Expr and keyword transparent at every profile. Measured consequence: charge(ChargeParam(target_voltage=4.2, c_rate=0.23)) restored as ChargeParam(4.2, 0.23) and the loop body flattened to one line. Named arguments silently became positional, which is a semantic change, and the collapse could then never fire because keyword.arg was gone. ast now drops only positions and empty lists, both of which the decoder reconstructs, so it round-trips.

keyword is never transparent, it folds. Folding merges it into the parent Call as keywordArguments: {name: value}, preserving the name and setting argumentIndex: -1 plus argumentName. This is the analysis's "collapsing keyword into a dict on the Call", which preserves rather than discards.

A third condition is content-dependent and lives in M6: a call collapses if and only if its callee resolves to an annotated type.

items.title: Ambient vocabulary
items.text:
Owned here, as data. The principle transfers from Graphify; the contents invert, because Graphify's lists encode what a repository is about and these must encode what a workflow is about. Graphify lists dataclass as noise; here an annotated base class is signal.

Start deliberately small and grow from evidence on the real corpus file, which is roughly half matplotlib. Over-filtering strips meaningful calls; under-filtering fills the graph with plotting.

items.title: Non-goals
items.text: • Not a walker. Applying these sets is M5.

import ast

from awl.vocab import NODE_TYPES, node_type_for


def test_every_ast_node_type_maps_to_the_vocabulary():
    """No node may be silently unmapped. Unknown is a legitimate answer."""
    unmapped = [
        name
        for name in dir(ast)
        if isinstance(getattr(ast, name), type)
        and issubclass(getattr(ast, name), ast.AST)
        and node_type_for(name) not in NODE_TYPES
    ]
    assert not unmapped, f"unmapped: {unmapped}"


def test_an_unrecognised_node_is_Unknown_not_an_error():
    """The tripwire is explicit, because .get() cannot raise.

    A new Python version adding a node type must surface as Unknown here, and
    the mapping table extended deliberately.
    """
    assert node_type_for("SomeFuturePython315Node") == "Unknown"

Run: uv run python -m pytest tests/test_vocab.py -v Expected: FAIL, ModuleNotFoundError

  • [ ] Step 3: Write the implementation
"""Language-neutral node vocabulary, orderings, profiles and noise lists.

Pure data. Modelled on Joern's Code Property Graph so a second language
frontend does not require a second vocabulary.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from types import MappingProxyType

__all__ = [
    "NODE_TYPES", "PROFILES", "TRANSPARENT", "OPAQUE", "FOLDS_KEYWORDS",
    "ORDERED_FIELDS", "AMBIENT_CALLEES", "AMBIENT_ANNOTATIONS",
    "node_type_for", "operator_name_for",
]

NODE_TYPES = frozenset({
    "Method", "Block", "Call", "ControlStructure", "Identifier", "Literal",
    "Local", "Return", "TypeDecl", "Type", "Member", "Unknown",
})

_BY_NODE = MappingProxyType({
    "FunctionDef": "Method", "AsyncFunctionDef": "Method", "Lambda": "Method",
    "Module": "Block", "Interactive": "Block", "Expression": "Block",
    "Call": "Call",
    "If": "ControlStructure", "While": "ControlStructure", "For": "ControlStructure",
    "AsyncFor": "ControlStructure", "With": "ControlStructure", "AsyncWith": "ControlStructure",
    "Try": "ControlStructure", "TryStar": "ControlStructure", "Match": "ControlStructure",
    "Break": "ControlStructure", "Continue": "ControlStructure",
    "Name": "Identifier",
    "Constant": "Literal", "JoinedStr": "Literal", "FormattedValue": "Literal",
    "Return": "Return", "Yield": "Return", "YieldFrom": "Return", "Await": "Return",
    "ClassDef": "TypeDecl", "AnnAssign": "Member",
    "Assign": "Call", "AugAssign": "Call", "BinOp": "Call", "BoolOp": "Call",
    "UnaryOp": "Call", "Compare": "Call", "Attribute": "Call", "Subscript": "Call",
})

_OPERATORS = MappingProxyType({
    "Assign": "<operator>.assignment", "AnnAssign": "<operator>.assignment",
    "AugAssign": "<operator>.assignmentPlus",
    "Add": "<operator>.addition", "Sub": "<operator>.subtraction",
    "Mult": "<operator>.multiplication", "Div": "<operator>.division",
    "Mod": "<operator>.modulo", "Pow": "<operator>.exponentiation",
    "Eq": "<operator>.equals", "NotEq": "<operator>.notEquals",
    "Lt": "<operator>.lessThan", "LtE": "<operator>.lessEqualsThan",
    "Gt": "<operator>.greaterThan", "GtE": "<operator>.greaterEqualsThan",
    "And": "<operator>.logicalAnd", "Or": "<operator>.logicalOr",
    "Not": "<operator>.logicalNot",
    "Attribute": "<operator>.fieldAccess", "Subscript": "<operator>.indexAccess",
})


def node_type_for(ast_node_name: str) -> str:
    """Return the neutral node type for a Python AST node type name."""
    return _BY_NODE.get(ast_node_name, "Unknown")


def operator_name_for(ast_node_name: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the reserved call name for an operator node, or None."""
    return _OPERATORS.get(ast_node_name)


# Statement lists whose order is semantic, so M5 materializes an index on them.
ORDERED_FIELDS = ("body", "orelse", "finalbody")

_WRAPPERS = frozenset({"Expr", "arguments", "alias"})

TRANSPARENT = MappingProxyType({
    # ast elides nothing structural, so it round-trips. See the profile note.
    "ast": frozenset(),
    "workflow": _WRAPPERS,
    "provenance": _WRAPPERS,
    "signature": _WRAPPERS,
})

# keyword is never transparent: folding preserves the argument name.
FOLDS_KEYWORDS = MappingProxyType({
    "ast": False, "workflow": True, "provenance": True, "signature": True,
})

_EXPRESSIONS = frozenset({
    "BinOp", "BoolOp", "UnaryOp", "Compare",
    "ListComp", "DictComp", "SetComp", "GeneratorExp",
})

OPAQUE = MappingProxyType({
    "ast": frozenset(),
    "workflow": _EXPRESSIONS,
    "provenance": _EXPRESSIONS,
    "signature": _EXPRESSIONS,
})

PROFILES = tuple(TRANSPARENT)

# Ambient vocabulary: shared by every workflow, so it distinguishes nothing.
# Deliberately small. Grow it from evidence on the real corpus file, not from
# Graphify's lists, which encode what a repository is about.
AMBIENT_CALLEES = frozenset({
    "print", "len", "range", "enumerate", "zip", "isinstance", "getattr",
    "str", "int", "float", "bool", "list", "dict", "set", "tuple",
})

AMBIENT_ANNOTATIONS = frozenset({
    "Optional", "Union", "List", "Dict", "Any", "Sequence", "Iterable",
    "str", "int", "float", "bool", "bytes", "None",
})
  • [ ] Step 4: Run the test, then commit
uv run python -m pytest tests/test_vocab.py -v
git add src/awl/vocab.py tests/test_vocab.py
git commit -m "feat(vocab): add the language-neutral node vocabulary"

items.title: Task 2: Keep the vocabulary closed, neutral, and the profiles distinct
items.text:
• [ ] Step 1: Write the tests
import pytest

from awl.vocab import (
    FOLDS_KEYWORDS, NODE_TYPES, OPAQUE, PROFILES, TRANSPARENT,
    node_type_for, operator_name_for,
)


def test_the_vocabulary_is_closed():
    assert len(NODE_TYPES) == 12


def test_control_flow_uses_one_type_with_a_discriminator():
    for name in ("If", "While", "For", "Try", "Match", "Break"):
        assert node_type_for(name) == "ControlStructure"


def test_no_vocabulary_name_is_python_specific():
    assert not (NODE_TYPES & {"AugAssign", "Expr", "arguments", "keyword", "Constant", "Name"})


def test_operators_are_calls_with_reserved_names():
    assert node_type_for("BinOp") == "Call"
    assert operator_name_for("Add") == "<operator>.addition"
    assert operator_name_for("AugAssign") == "<operator>.assignmentPlus"
    assert operator_name_for("Call") is None


def test_the_ast_profile_elides_nothing_structural():
    """Guards the regression that turned named arguments into positional ones."""
    assert TRANSPARENT["ast"] == frozenset()
    assert OPAQUE["ast"] == frozenset()
    assert FOLDS_KEYWORDS["ast"] is False


def test_keyword_is_never_transparent():
    """Folding preserves the argument name; transparency destroyed it."""
    for profile in PROFILES:
        assert "keyword" not in TRANSPARENT[profile]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("profile", ["workflow", "provenance", "signature"])
def test_reduced_profiles_fold_keywords(profile):
    assert FOLDS_KEYWORDS[profile] is True

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:
• [ ] Every ast node type resolves to a member of NODE_TYPES, with Unknown as an explicit, tested fallback.
  • [ ] The vocabulary contains no Python-specific name and has exactly 12 members.
  • [ ] TRANSPARENT["ast"] and OPAQUE["ast"] are empty, and ast does not fold keywords.
  • [ ] keyword is transparent in no profile.
  • [ ] Ambient-noise lists exist here, not in a walker.
  • [ ] tests/test_vocab.py imports only awl.vocab.

items.title: Known limits
items.text:
• The operator table is not exhaustive over 13 binary and 10 comparison operators. operator_name_for returning None is the signal to extend it, which keeps vocabulary decisions out of the walker.
  • Local and Type have no direct ast node and are assigned by position, so M5 sets them; the table alone cannot.
  • provenance and signature currently share workflow's sets. Their distinguishing behaviour (typed boundaries only, declarations only) is not expressible as a node-type set and needs a predicate M5 supplies. Until then those two profiles are aliases, and M5's test asserts only signature <= workflow.

items.title: M2 awl.ids implementation plan
items.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: One place that mints identities, so every producer in the system agrees on what a given code entity is called.

Architecture: Pure functions over a declarative configuration. Identity minting is data (a path-pattern to namespace map, Kythe's vnames.json pattern), not code. Identity for an OO-LD class follows a declared precedence that mirrors get_cls_iri(), so AWL-LD and oold cannot disagree.

Tech Stack: Python stdlib only.

items.title: Contract
items.text: Consumes identity parts, and the type declarations M3 extracts Produces Identity (identity.schema.json) Depends on awl.contracts only

items.title: Why this is one module and not a helper
items.text:
From graphify/ids.py, whose docstring states the failure directly:

Three independent producers must agree on node IDs or the graph splits a single entity into disconnected ghost nodes.

AWL-LD has the same three producers: the AST walk (M3), the collapse (M6) and the RDF projection (M8). It is worse here than in Graphify, because these identifiers are global IRIs rather than graph-local ids: a collision is a wrong assertion about the world, not a merged node in one tool's database.

items.title: Identity precedence for a class
items.text:
Verified against the OO-LD spec, spec/sections/07-schema-instances.md.

  1. x-oold-instance-rdf-type on the schema. A list, because it co-types: it lists every rdf:type an instance asserts at once. Under allOf the nearest declaration is authoritative and replaces a base class's value rather than appending (rule OOLD-INS-559f).
  2. The inline type field default, e.g. "ex:Person" or ["Diameter"]. If both are present the inline value MUST be consistent with the schema declaration (rule OOLD-INS-4b5c).
  3. The import path, when no IRI is declared at all.

items.title: Identity is the typed instantiation, not the function
items.text:
The refinement that makes opaque callees tractable. scipy.stats.linregress is generic linear regression; attaching (LinearStrain, Stress) -> ModulusOfElasticity to that identifier asserts it for every use of linregress on earth. The semantics belong to the typed instantiation:

scipy.stats.linregress                        no semantics, ever
scipy.stats.linregress(LinearStrain, Stress)  -> ModulusOfElasticity

This is what SCIP's method-disambiguator and Kythe's opaque signature field exist for. With OO-LD types on the arguments the instantiation is derivable statically at every call site, so a model is needed once to propose the mapping and dispatch afterwards is deterministic.

Retroactive minting. Kythe's entry store is append-only facts keyed by VName, so any analyzer may add facts later and they join everywhere the symbol was referenced. Mint the identifier for an opaque callee now; attach semantics whenever they become known; every prior reference gains meaning without reprocessing. That property is the reason identity must be stable and global before anything else is built.

items.title: Versioning
items.text: Decided: OO-LD classes may carry a version, from x-oold-version or a versioned $id. Other assets usually do not. Record a distribution version where package metadata is inspectable; leave the slot empty otherwise rather than guessing. Environment pinning (a Dockerfile or devcontainer) cannot be derived from Python source and is therefore not part of extraction; if a repository has one, a human or an agent assigns it on top of the extracted graph as a separate layer. The contract leaves room for that but this module does not populate it.

items.title: Non-goals
items.text:
• Not resolution. Deciding which identity a local name refers to is M4.
  • Not extraction. Reading declarations out of source is M3.
